units.function: Pure policy for suppressing repeated no-information Issue wakes after consecutive successful Runs produce no Issue-visible progress, with typed actor exceptions and capped exponential cooldown.
units.dependencyDirection: Standalone service exports constants, string taxonomies and pure functions; callers must query and order tenant/Agent/Issue-scoped Runs/activity, evaluate the decision and enqueue or suppress work.
units.keyDataModels: Wake candidate intent and actor; progress/new-input activity action sets; recent terminal Run sample; no-progress streak; cooldown/last finish/next-allowed decision.
units.lifecycle: Caller classifies a wake -> supplies newest-first same-Agent/same-Issue history and progress/input facts -> service resets or counts no-progress Runs -> blocks until escalating cooldown expires or returns allow -> server recovery paths bypass this gate.
units.testAssessment: The paired 14-test pure suite passed. It exercises classification, human/Agent distinctions, escalation bypass, cooldown threshold/cap/expiry and reset paths. Integration evidence remains necessary for scoped history selection, atomic queue suppression, concurrency, durable receipts, clock skew and complete safety-event classification.
units.designRationale: A documented recovery smoke incurred 25 adapter sessions and 2.4x cost for one stalled recovery, so unchanged polling needs explicit backpressure without slowing genuine human/event/recovery input.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must bound runaway Agent and Connector costs, prevent wake storms and expose why work was delayed, while never delaying accountable-human control or masking a required approval.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT this as a vendor-neutral RetryBackpressurePolicy, retaining narrow visible-progress semantics, bounded sampling and capped backoff. Replace strings with versioned WakeIntent/ProgressKind, scope inputs by tenant/Work/Agent/Connector, persist policy version and ThrottleReceipt, use transactional idempotent scheduling with jitter, and declare HumanDecision/Approval/Revocation/EmergencyStop as non-throttleable types.
units.responsibilityConflict: Responsibility safety depends entirely on callers supplying correctly scoped history and classifying events. Agent-authored resumes are deliberately delayed, and there is no authoritative receipt or policy snapshot explaining suppression to an accountable human.
units.securityFindings: HIGH caller-trust boundary: the module cannot verify tenant/Work/Agent scoping or newest-first ordering. HIGH safety taxonomy risk: string allowlists determine whether human control signals are delayed. MEDIUM audit gap: suppression is not represented as a durable receipt here. MEDIUM distributed-systems gap: no atomic queue decision, concurrency, jitter or clock/fencing semantics. POSITIVE: overflow cap, failure/new-input resets, human wake privilege and narrow progress evidence directly address a real cost/storm failure mode.
